questions.stem: Why does iron rust faster in salt water than in pure water?

options.text: Salt reacts directly with iron to form rust
Salt removes the protective oxide layer from iron
Salt water is a better electrical conductor, allowing the electrochemical rusting reactions to happen faster
Salt water contains more oxygen than pure water

questions.explanation: Salt water is a better electrical conductor than pure water. Since rusting is an electrochemical process involving electron transfer (Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻), the improved conductivity allows electrons to transfer more easily, speeding up the rusting reactions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a barrier method of preventing rust?

options.text: Attaching blocks of zinc to a ship's hull
Making the iron into stainless steel

questions.explanation: Painting is a barrier method because the paint forms a physical coating that keeps water and oxygen away from the iron surface, preventing rusting. Attaching zinc blocks and magnesium anodes are examples of sacrificial protection, while stainless steel is an example of alloying.
